title: Fernando Alonso to race in 2027 Dakar Rally with Aston Martin
content:
Fernando Alonso will make a second attempt to win the Dakar Rally in January 2027, with the Aston Martin brand he represents in Formula 1.

The double F1 world champion will drive an Aston Martin Dreadnought truck in the two-week event held in Portugal and Morocco early next year. It will cover nearly 2,700 miles, over 12 daily stages between 220 and 310 miles in length.

The 2027 Dakar shifted location from Saudi Arabia as a consequence of the Iran War and ongoing uncertainty in the Middle East.

It will be the second time Alonso, 45, has attempted to win the rally after he entered the 2020 edition with Toyota. The rally was first held as an ultra-endurance motorsport test between Paris in France and Dakar in Senegal between 1979-2007 before its location first shifted due to the threat of terrorist attacks on the original route.

Alonso’s first Dakar entry was during his F1 sabbatical between 2019 and 2021. He returned to race for Alpine in 2021 before joining Aston in 2023. The 2027 Dakar will be the first entry for Aston — best known as a premium sports car brand. It re-signed Alonso to a new F1 contract in September.

In the two years where he did not race in F1, Alonso contested several of the biggest races in wider motorsport.

He won the 24 Hours of Le Mans twice (his first triumph came in 2018 when he completed a dual program with his then main employer McLaren in F1 and Toyota in the World Endurance Championship, which he won overall in its 2018-2019 campaign) and the 24 Hours of Daytona.

Alonso was less successful in his other ventures during his F1 hiatus. He failed to qualify for the 2019 Indianapolis 500 and finished a lap down in 2020, after making a first appearance (again with McLaren’s blessing) in 2017, where he retired.

In the 2020 Dakar Rally, Alonso finished 13th overall — over four-and-half hours behind winner Carlos Sainz (father of Williams F1 driver, Carlos Sainz).

Alonso’s rally featured a long delay to get repairs on the second stage and a roll on the 10th stage. He did not win a stage — the daily individual contests that make up the rally’s overall contest.

“After deciding to continue racing in F1 with the Aston Martin, I thought carefully about Dakar,” Alonso said in an Aston press release. “In the end, the decision became simple. I wanted to embrace the challenge completely and take on both F1 and the Dakar Rally in the same year.

Alonso’s co-driver on the 2027 Dakar will be five-time motorcycle category winner Marc Coma. Sébastien Loeb, the nine-time World Rally champion, will pilot another Dreadnought in the event — one of three being entered.

The truck was first featured as a digital vehicle in the 2026 video game, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

Alonso added: “F1 remains my priority. But I am a racing driver, and challenges like this are why I love competing. I’m looking forward to seeing what we can achieve.”
